subject: business-studies
title: Business Basics & Startup Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the building blocks of business — aims, sectors and the legal forms a startup can take.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies foundations — business aims, the three sectors and legal structures explained.
final_note: You learned why businesses exist, the three sectors of the economy, and the main legal structures owners can choose.

concepts.def: A long-term goal a business wants to achieve
Provides services to consumers and businesses
Two or more owners sharing profits and risk

walkthroughs.body_html:
Every business has aims — long-term goals it tries to achieve.

Common aims include making a profit, surviving, growing, helping a social cause, and being independent.

The economy is split into three sectors.

Primary extracts raw materials (a farm). Secondary turns them into goods (a bakery). Tertiary provides services (a hairdresser).

A sole trader is the simplest form — one person, full control, but full unlimited liability if it fails.

A partnership shares the load between 2+ owners but disputes can happen and liability is still unlimited.

mcqs.q: Which sector does a coal mine belong to?
options: Primary
Secondary
Tertiary
Quaternary

mcqs.q: What does 'unlimited liability' mean for a sole trader?
options: They can borrow unlimited money
Personal assets can be taken to pay business debts
They pay no tax
They can hire unlimited staff

mcqs.q: What is a key disadvantage of being a sole trader?
options: The main disadvantage is that sole traders can't sell any products.
Sole traders must employ at least one other person by law.
Unlimited liability — the owner's personal assets are at risk if the business fails, because there is no legal separation between owner and business.
Primary research is done first and secondary research is done later.

mcqs.q: Which sector does manufacturing belong to?
options: The secondary sector — which transforms raw materials from the primary sector (farming, mining) into finished goods.
Manufacturing is in the tertiary sector along with services.
Manufacturing is in the primary sector because it makes things.
Primary research is done first and secondary research is done later.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary market research?
options: Sole traders must employ at least one other person by law.
Primary research is done first and secondary research is done later.
Primary research is original data the business gathers itself (surveys, interviews); secondary research uses existing data (reports, government statistics, market intelligence).
Primary research is the most important and secondary research is less important.
